concerns.text: The plan cites 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/ethanolivertroy/nist-cybersecurity-training/resolve/main/embeddings/train_embeddings.parquet' as the 'NIST Adsorption Database'. This URL points to a cybersecurity training dataset (embeddings), not adsorption isotherm data. The dataset is completely inappropriate for the research question (predicting Langmuir/Henry parameters from molecular features). The plan must cite a real, accessible source containing adsorption isotherm measurements (e.g., the actual NIST ISODB or a verified MOF-adsorption repository).

The plan states 'NO verified source found' for the MOF-1000 Zenodo repository and explicitly excludes it from modeling. Since the project relies on adsorbent properties (surface area, pore volume) which are not present in the (incorrectly cited) NIST URL, the current data strategy leaves the project with zero valid data for the adsorbent features required by FR-001 and the spec. The plan must identify a valid, accessible source for MOF adsorption data or revise the scope to exclude adsorbent property prediction.

The plan proposes leveraging 'Kaggle’s free tier' for GPU acceleration if necessary. This violates the 'free-model + free-compute' constraints of the llmXive environment which assumes execution on the project's CI runner (GitHub Actions). Relying on an external, unmanaged free tier (Kaggle) introduces a non-deterministic dependency and breaks the reproducibility requirement (Constitution Principle I) as the CI runner cannot access external user accounts or free-tier quotas.
